pinpoints.change: The `for (let index = 0; index < dataResources_.length; index++)` loop calls `setState(index, unwrap(unwrappedResult))` per slot, so results are overwritten in place and never removed; make the store equal the new result array instead (e.g. `setState(reconcile(...))`).

`createRenderEffect(on(() => queriesOptions().queries.length, () => setState(observer.getOptimisticResult(...)[1]()))` merges the new array by index without truncating; it must shrink `state` to the new length.
`createRenderEffect(() => setProxyState(getProxies()))` writes the proxy array into the existing store slot-by-slot, so stale proxies for removed queries stay reactive and rendered.

Owns the converge-in-both-directions contract: `difference(prevObservers, newObservers).forEach((observer) => observer.destroy())` plus `this.#result = newResult`; the adapter projections must mirror this removal half.
`replaceAt` only substitutes at an existing index — the length-changing path is `setQueries`, so consumers must not treat per-index notification as the whole update.
Declares the symmetry the projection must honour — `added?: Set<T>` and `removed?: Set<T>` — removals are as much a part of an update as insertions.
